ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF EAST HALMAHERA REGENCY
NUMBER 7 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in East Halmahera so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in East Halmahera.

Article 5
(1) In order to improve the position, role, and quality of women, as well as efforts to realize gender equality and justice in family life, society, nation, and state, women must be empowered.
(2) The empowerment of women as referred to in paragraph (1) is directed towards obtaining opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in economic, socio-cultural, political, and legal activities.
Article 6 (1) Regional Governments have the obligation and responsibility in efforts to empower women.
(2) Efforts to empower women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the prevailing laws and regulations.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of East Halmahera Regency.

18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.

Article 33
Other violence as referred to in Article 27 letter f is caused by:
a. threat of violence includes: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and
b. coercion, includes: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something that is contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Region of East Halmahera Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Government of East Halmahera Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of East Halmahera.
4. Regional Apparatus is the supporting element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of Government Affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the affairs of Women's Empowerment and/or Child Protection.
6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
7. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
8. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social abilities, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective capabilities.
9. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering either physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom.
11. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
12. Protection is all preventive actions, services and empowerment to protect and guarantee the rights of women and children from acts of violence.
13. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
14. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
15. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
16. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and naturally both in the family and in society.
17. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
18. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to their area of origin.
19. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2PTP2A, is the Regional Technical Implementation Unit (UPTDD) of the Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children integrated into the technical Regional Apparatus of East Halmahera Regency.

6.1.rationale: The original Indonesian Pasal 11 ayat (1) huruf h-i mentions protection of women (including victims of violence, female workers, elderly women, women with disabilities) “di daerah konflik dan daerah yang terkena bencana” (in conflict areas and disaster-affected areas). However, this appears within a broad gender-mainstreaming list and does not set out specific VAW/GBV measures tailored to crisis/humanitarian settings (services, protocols, response in emergencies). If the indicator ‘Women in crisis settings’ expects explicit crisis-setting VAW provisions, the judge over-read a general clause as satisfying it, producing a false positive.

6.3.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly recognizes women’s right to work and to fair remuneration and treatment in employment relations, indicating specific attention to women workers.

NUMBER 7 OF 2022
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. In order to prevent and overcome violence against women and children in East Halmahera so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children victims of violence in the form of regional regulations. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children victims of violence have not yet regulated protection measures at the Regional level, therefore institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee their implementation. Regional Regulations regulate protection measures for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services and empowerment of women and children victims of violence in East Halmahera.

CHAPTER VII

Article 50
(1) To ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities, protection of Women and children, the Government conducts monitoring.
(2) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the technical Regional Apparatus and P2TP2A.
(3) Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children.
(4) Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus that implement policies, activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence.
(5) Monitoring is conducted starting from planning up to the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children every year.

Article 51
(1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and children victims of violence shall be conducted at the end of each Fiscal year or if necessary according to needs.
(2) The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence shall be used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the protection of Women and children victims of violence for the following year.
(3) Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

6.3.rationale: The original Indonesian Pasal 4 lists general women’s human rights, including the right “untuk bekerja serta mendapat imbalan dan perlakuan yang adil dan layak” (to work and receive fair remuneration and treatment). This is not an intersectional VAW-focused provision targeting women workers as a vulnerable group (contrast with Pasal 11 which explicitly lists “tenaga kerja perempuan” in protection measures). The judge treated a general right-to-work clause as ‘women workers’ intersectional approach, which is too broad for the indicator, leading to a false positive.

6.4.evaluator_rationale: The policy explicitly mentions organizing protection of women including “elderly women,” indicating targeted protection measures for this group.
